questions.q: Which three conditions define weak (covariance) stationarity?
options: Constant mean, constant variance, and autocovariance depending only on lag (not on time)
Zero mean, zero variance, and a unit root
Normally distributed values, zero skew, and zero kurtosis
Monotonically increasing mean and constant variance
questions.explain: Weak stationarity requires constant mean, constant variance, and an autocovariance structure that depends only on the lag between observations, not on the specific time index.

questions.q: In the AR(1) model X_t = phi * X_(t-1) + eps_t, what happens when phi = 1?
options: The process becomes white noise
The process becomes a random walk with a unit root; shocks never decay and variance grows without bound
The process becomes perfectly stationary
The process is undefined and cannot be simulated
questions.explain: When phi = 1, X_t = X_(t-1) + eps_t, the defining equation of a random walk. This is the canonical unit-root process: past shocks have a permanent effect and variance grows over time.

questions.q: What is the null hypothesis (H0) of the Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) test?
options: The series is stationary
The series has a unit root (it is non-stationary)
The series is white noise
The series has zero mean
questions.explain: The ADF test's null hypothesis is that the series has a unit root, i.e., it is non-stationary. This is a common point of confusion — many assume stationarity is the null by default.

questions.q: A quant runs adfuller() on a price series and gets a p-value of 0.62. What should they conclude?
options: Reject H0 — the series is stationary
Fail to reject H0 — the series appears non-stationary, consistent with price levels behaving like a random walk
The test is inconclusive and must be discarded
The series definitely has no unit root
questions.explain: A p-value of 0.62 is well above common significance thresholds (e.g., 0.05), so the null hypothesis of a unit root (non-stationarity) cannot be rejected — exactly the expected result for raw price levels.

questions.q: What does the 'Augmented' in Augmented Dickey-Fuller refer to?
options: Testing multiple series simultaneously
Adding lagged difference terms to the regression to remove residual autocorrelation beyond the basic Dickey-Fuller test
Augmenting the sample size using bootstrap resampling
Converting prices to log returns before testing
questions.explain: The original Dickey-Fuller test includes no lagged difference terms. The Augmented version adds enough lagged differences (often chosen via a criterion like AIC) to account for higher-order autocorrelation in the residuals.
